Mechanical Engineering Graduate Program
Admission to PhD program
Thank you for your interest in the doctoral program in the Department of Mechanical Engineering. Below you will find the information required to apply for the Fall 2027 admission cycle.
Link to PhD Program
Application Deadlines
Priority Deadline: February 15, 2027
We will continue to accept and evaluate applications on a rolling basis after the priority deadline.
How to Apply All application materials must be submitted online through the Link.
Required Application Materials A complete application must include the following documents:
Statement of Purpose
Official transcripts from all undergraduate and graduate institutions attended
Resume or Curriculum Vitae (CV)
Three letters of recommendation
Minimum Qualifications for Applicants
Academic Record: A minimum grade average of B (e.g., 3.0 on a 4.0 scale, 60/100, or 13/20).
English Language Proficiency: Applicants from countries where English is not the primary language must submit TOEFL scores.
GRE Requirement The GRE requirement is suspended for the Fall 2026 application cycle. Please do not send GRE scores, as they will not be considered in the application review process.
Financial Support All students admitted to our Ph.D. program will be offered full financial support, which includes a stipend and tuition waiver, through a Research Assistantship and/or a Teaching Assistantship.
Contacting Faculty We strongly encourage prospective students to contact the faculty members they are interested in working with to inquire about potential openings in their research labs.
Additional Information & Inquiries
For any specific inquiries, please contact the Ph.D. Program Advisor, Prof. Taehun Lee.
Admission to Master's program
This page provides application information for prospective Master's students. We offer paths for both degree-seeking and non-degree students.
Link to MS Program
Application Deadlines
For Degree-Seeking Students:
Fall Admission: May 1
Spring Admission: November 15
For Non-Degree Students:
Applications are evaluated on a rolling basis. Please contact the MS Program Advisor for more information.
How to Apply All candidates must submit their application and supporting documents through the Link.
Application Requirements A complete application must include the following:
Required Documents:
Statement of Purpose
Official transcripts from all colleges and universities attended
Resume or Curriculum Vitae (CV)
Two letters of recommendation
Minimum Qualifications:
Academic Record: A scholastic record showing a minimum grade average of B (e.g., 3.0 on a 4.0 scale).
English Language Proficiency: Applicants from countries where English is not the primary language must submit TOEFL scores. The minimum required scores are 533 (Paper-Based) or 73 (Internet-Based).
Resources and Inquiries
To learn about the program curriculum, view the Link.
For any further inquiries, please contact the MS Program Advisor, Prof. Niell Elvin.
